name: Massage Therapy Licensing Exam (MBLEx)

issuer.name: Federation of State Massage Therapy Boards (FSMTB)

examInfo.format: The FSMTB Candidate Handbook describes the MBLEx as a computer-based test of 100 multiple choice questions taken in 110 minutes. It covers seven content areas: Anatomy & Physiology (11%), Kinesiology (12%), Pathology, Contraindications, Areas of Caution, Special Populations (14%), Benefits and Effects of Soft Tissue Manipulation (15%), Client Assessment, Reassessment & Treatment Planning (17%), Ethics, Boundaries, Laws & Regulations (16%), and Guidelines for Professional Practice (15%). This practice mock uses 4 answer choices per question.

passCriteria.description: The real MBLEx is scored on a scale from 300 to 900, and a scaled score of 630 is the passing score. A scaled score is not a percent of correct answers. This site uses 70% correct as a practice goal only; it is not an official cut score. There is no separate minimum score for each content area.

content.eligibility: Your state massage therapy board decides who may take the MBLEx, including required school hours. Most candidates apply through FSMTB after their state approves them. Check your state board and the FSMTB Candidate Handbook before you apply.
content.intro: The MBLEx is the national licensing exam that most U.S. state boards use for massage therapists. It has 100 multiple choice questions in 110 minutes across seven content areas, from anatomy and kinesiology to ethics, client assessment, and safe practice. Short practice sets here help you review muscles and joints, contraindications, the effects of massage, and the rules that keep clients safe.
content.trendSummary: Client Assessment, Reassessment & Treatment Planning is the largest content area at 17%, followed by Ethics, Boundaries, Laws & Regulations at 16%. Kinesiology asks about muscle attachments, actions, and joint movements. Pathology questions focus on when massage is contraindicated and how to adapt a session. The chapters on this site are study groupings of the official content areas, and the chapter splits are estimates, not official numbers.
content.studyTip: Start with Anatomy & Physiology and Kinesiology, because many assessment and pathology questions build on them. Then learn contraindications and the effects of massage, and finish with ethics and professional practice. When you can answer most Intermediate questions, take a full 100-question Mock Exam and review every miss.

faqs.question: How many questions are on the MBLEx?
faqs.answer: The MBLEx has 100 multiple choice questions, and you get 110 minutes to answer them.

faqs.question: What score do I need to pass the MBLEx?
faqs.answer: Scores range from 300 to 900, and a scaled score of 630 passes. A scaled score is not the same as a percent correct. This site uses 70% correct as a practice goal.

faqs.question: What topics does the MBLEx cover?
faqs.answer: Seven content areas: Anatomy & Physiology (11%), Kinesiology (12%), Pathology, Contraindications, Areas of Caution, Special Populations (14%), Benefits and Effects of Soft Tissue Manipulation (15%), Client Assessment, Reassessment & Treatment Planning (17%), Ethics, Boundaries, Laws & Regulations (16%), and Guidelines for Professional Practice (15%).

faqs.question: Are these the real MBLEx questions?
faqs.answer: No. Every question here is an AI-made practice question written for study. Real exam questions are confidential, so use this site for practice and also study your school's materials and the official FSMTB resources.

faqs.question: Is this site connected to FSMTB?
faqs.answer: No. This site is independent and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by FSMTB or any state board.

studyTips.studyOrder: Start with Anatomy & Physiology (11 questions) and Kinesiology (12 questions), because muscles, joints, and body systems come up again in pathology and assessment. Next study Pathology, Contraindications, Areas of Caution, Special Populations (14) and Benefits and Effects of Soft Tissue Manipulation (15). Finish with the three practice areas: Client Assessment, Reassessment & Treatment Planning (17), Ethics, Boundaries, Laws & Regulations (16), and Guidelines for Professional Practice (15).
studyTips.hardChapters: Muscles: Attachments and Actions asks you to match each muscle with its origin, insertion, and action, so learn them in small groups by body region. Pathology and Contraindications asks when to skip a session and when to only avoid one area, so sort conditions into those two lists. In Ethics and Boundaries, transference, countertransference, and dual relationships are easy to mix up, so learn each with a simple example.
studyTips.examDay: The MBLEx has 100 questions in 110 minutes, so you have a little over one minute per question. Read "NOT" and "EXCEPT" questions twice. When a question asks what to do, choose the answer that keeps the client safe, stays within your scope of practice, and respects the client's consent. Mark hard questions in your head and keep a steady pace so you reach the end.
